title: BSA Incorporated
description: The Boy Scouts of America (BSA) is officially incorporated in Washington, D.C., by Chicago publisher W. D. Boyce after his encounter with the famous 'Unknown Scout' in London.

title: Lord Baden-Powell's Birth
description: Robert Baden-Powell, founder of the worldwide Scouting movement and Chief Scout of the World, is born in London, England. His birthday is celebrated globally as Founder's Day.

title: Woodrow Wilson Signs BSA Charter
description: U.S. President Woodrow Wilson signs a bill granting a federal charter to the Boy Scouts of America, protecting its name, insignia, and granting it special federal recognition.

title: James E. West Leads Organization
description: James E. West, who would become the first Chief Scout Executive of the BSA, begins organizing national agencies to establish the BSA administrative headquarters in New York.

title: BSA First Executive Meeting
description: Thirty-four prominent national representatives of boys' work agencies meet in New York to formalize organizational plans and establish the permanent structure of the BSA.

title: First Scout Camp Opens
description: Robert Baden-Powell opens the experimental camp on Brownsea Island, England, with 20 boys. The camp tests the patrol system, woodcraft, and pioneering, starting the global Scouting movement.

title: First Eagle Scout Awarded
description: Arthur Rose Eldred of Oceanside, New York, is officially awarded the first-ever Eagle Scout rank in BSA history, setting a standard of achievement for generations of Scouts.

title: Scouting for Boys Distributed
description: Robert Baden-Powell's landmark book 'Scouting for Boys' finishes its initial serial run and is printed in bound editions, rapidly sparking interest and leading to spontaneous scout troops.

title: Jamboree Planning Begins
description: The International Scouting Commissioner's Office starts formal planning for the 1st World Scout Jamboree, designed to unite young people globally after the devastation of World War I.
